name: Avon Lake Sheet Metal Company, Inc.
old_description: Avon Lake Sheet Metal Company, Inc. has been family-owned and operated since 1953 and conveniently located in Avon Lake, about 25 miles outside of Cleveland. As a leader in metal fabrication, we fabricate high-quality products to suit your needs, while also offering on-site installation and plant maintenance services to our customers, with safety always being one of our top priorities.
about:
Avon Lake Sheet Metal Company, Inc. was founded in 1953 by George Wightman and Carl Wetzig Sr. in a one-car garage in Avon Lake, Ohio, about 25 miles west of Cleveland. The business has remained family-owned through three generations, with second-generation owners Carl Wetzig Jr. and Gary Wightman now the company.

The company operates a 32,000-square-foot facility on a five-acre industrial site, equipped with CNC laser cutting (Trumpf 4 kW fiber laser), CNC plasma cutting, CNC press brake forming, CNC panel folding, plate rolling, and a range of welding processes including pulsed MIG, TIG, stick, and flux-core. In-house capabilities cover sheet metal and structural fabrication, assembly of mechanical components and modules, finishing such as painting and laser etching, and 3D modeling using Autodesk Inventor. The shop also provides industrial contracting services, including equipment installation, plant maintenance, project management, and coordination drawings.

Avon Lake Sheet Metal serves industries such as automotive, steel and foundry, chemical, plastics, construction, food processing, general manufacturing, retail, education, and health care. Customers include industrial mills, foundries, food processing companies, and medical groups, with projects ranging from custom machine guarding and HVAC duct systems to dust collection and pneumatic conveying installations.

The founders built the business on honesty and hard work, values that remain central today. The company emphasizes a combined fabrication-and-installation model to reduce the burden of multiple contracts, maintains a union workforce with AWS-certified welders, and has earned SMACNA Zero Injury Awards in multiple years, reflecting a long-standing safety focus.

name: Axial Medical
old_description: From prototype to production, Axial Medical can support all of your medical device manufacturing needs. A partnership with Axial will get your products into the field on time and on budget.
about:
Axial Medical operates a 40,000-square-foot facility in Warminster, Pennsylvania, just outside Philadelphia. The current headquarters was custom-built in 2014 around the needs of the medical device industry. The company's ownership structure and founding year are not publicly disclosed.

The shop specializes in precision machining and assembly for medical devices, running over 60 five-axis CNC mills—including Mazak, Haas, and Chiron machines—alongside Fanuc wire EDMs capable of 72-hour unmanned runs. In-line gun drilling serves cannulated products, while high-speed five-axis mills enable single-operation machining to tolerances of ±0.0001 inch. Optical and video inspection systems feed electronic data for statistical process control. The company also offers automated robotic cells, environmentally controlled assembly areas, and full validation of all in-house processes.

Axial serves medical device manufacturers, supporting projects from prototype through full-scale production. Its vendor-managed inventory programs and emphasis on risk mitigation cater to OEMs requiring regulated, traceable supply chains. The company highlights expertise in expandable implant production and complex assemblies.

The firm differentiates itself through its ISO 13485:2016 certification, FDA registration, and a continuous-improvement culture focused on part-per-bar yield optimization. Its "Made For Life" tagline reflects a commitment to delivering regulated components on time and on budget.

about:
Axiom Manufacturing operates from Richardson, Texas, where it has been building electronic assemblies since 1992. The company does business as Axiom Manufacturing under the Axent Manufacturing entity, though founder names and ownership structure are not disclosed publicly.

The shop focuses on printed circuit board assembly — both surface-mount and through-hole with automated optical inspection — alongside custom RF engineering that covers schematic capture, layout, and integration up to 40 GHz. It also provides full box-build electromechanical assembly and runs environmental, functional, and reliability testing to military standards. Over three decades the operation has shipped more than one million units to over five hundred customers.

Customers span aerospace and defense programs needing mission-critical aviation and space systems, industrial firms requiring ruggedized electronics for harsh environments, medical device makers who need FDA-compliant production, and telecom companies deploying high-frequency wireless infrastructure.

Axiom emphasizes a 98 percent on-time delivery rate and positions its combination of RF design depth, military-grade test protocols, and FDA-compliant processes as the reason it wins mission-critical work.

about:
Axles Plus operates from Beebe, Arkansas, where the company moved in 2017 after establishing the Axles Plus brand in Ward in 2015. The business traces its roots to 1979 when Custom Tool & Die, Inc. began in a small garage; it incorporated in April 1980 and has been based on Highway 5 near Cabot since 1982. Now in its third generation, the company remains family owned and operated.

The Cabot facility houses a full metal fabrication, tool and die, and manufacturing plant where production centers on CNC machining, laser cutting, metal fabrication, stamping, and custom manufacturing. At the Beebe location the team assembles trailer axles from scratch, prepares trucks for in‑state and out‑of‑state delivery, and runs a retail showroom stocked with tongue hitches, trailer jacks, axle bearings, LED clearance lights, brake lights, and bulk tires and wheels.

Axles Plus serves the trailer market broadly, building axles and components for equipment trailers, travel trailers, horse trailers, and other trailer types. Customers include both commercial trailer builders and individual owners who purchase parts directly from the showroom.

The company emphasizes that customer service and quality are non‑negotiable, positioning its American‑made, family‑run operation as a differentiator in a market where it says service still matters.

name: Axon Medical Technologies
old_description: is a powerful point-of-care platform that delivers a comprehensive range of
about:
Axon Medical Technologies operates from New Cumberland, Pennsylvania, where it was founded in 2003 by Michael Zarreii. Zarreii, who serves as chief executive and chief scientific officer, began the venture as a philanthropic effort to explore the link between the brain's involuntary sensory functions and cognition. His background spans electronics engineering, controls engineering, and continuing medical education in neurology at NYU's School of Medicine.

The company designs and manufactures two primary platforms in an FDA-registered U.S. facility: ECAT, a point-of-care multi-screening system that runs automated assessments for depression, anxiety, cognitive decline, TBI, PTSD, and ADHD; and Intellig-EYES, a lightweight headgear that captures 140 parameters of cranial nerve performance through advanced pupillometry. Tests include Trail Making A and B, GPCOG, MMSE, CAPS-5, and rapid sideline concussion screening. ECAT integrates with Epic, Cerner, and other EMRs, and the company employs a leasing model with per-scan billing supported by CPT codes for Medicare and private insurance reimbursement.

Axon Medical serves primary care clinics, military treatment facilities, and sports medicine programs. The U.S. Army has funded a four-year study to integrate both platforms into battlefield and hospital protocols, and the NCAA's chief medical officer sits on the advisory board alongside Army medical research colonels and university physicians. The technology addresses depression, anxiety, cognitive impairment, PTSD, concussions, and attention disorders.

Zarreii's motivation traces to the loss of his daughter Samira, after whom Intellig-EYES is named. The company invested 19 years and millions of dollars without government grants to develop non-invasive, objective diagnostics that generate clear reports in a single extended visit. Multiple patents have been issued with more pending, covering optics, stimuli generation, and measurement standards for autonomic nervous system assessment.

name: B & H Sheet Metal
old_description: Custom Fabrication of Steel, Stainless Steel, Aluminum and Copper.
about:
B & H Sheet Metal operates from Asheville, North Carolina, where it has served Western North Carolina since 1976. The business is a second‑generation, family‑owned and operated fabrication shop that began with rolling, bending, punching, press brake forming, and shearing work.

The company provides full‑service custom sheet metal fabrication, working with steel, stainless steel, aluminum, copper, and galvanized materials. Its capabilities include rolling, bending, punching, press brake forming, shearing, and welding. No products are pre‑fabricated; each job—from custom chimney caps to stainless steel countertops—is built to order for both residential and commercial clients. The shop emphasizes that no job is too large or too small.

Customers range from homeowners and contractors to commercial builders across Western North Carolina. Typical projects include architectural metalwork such as chimney caps, countertops, and other custom metal designs for residential and commercial construction.

The firm highlights its warranty on workmanship, free consultations, and over four decades of experience as differentiators. It stresses competitive pricing and the ability to deliver parts when needed, reflecting a commitment to quality materials and customer experience passed down through the family.

name: B & L Scales, Inc.
old_description: B&L Scales, Inc was founded in 1976 by C. Leroy McBride. Leroy began by traveling the state on his Goldwing Motorcycle, pulling a tiny trailer with his tools and necessities; visiting customers, servicing scales and machines, and building his business one stop at a time.
about:
B & L Scales, Inc. is based in Billings, Montana. Founded in 1976 by C. Leroy McBride, the company began as a one-man operation with McBride traveling the state on a Goldwing motorcycle, pulling a trailer of tools to service scales and equipment. The business remains family-owned; today it is operated by John and Nikki McFerran, with John continuing semi-annual service routes across Montana, Wyoming, and parts of Colorado while Nikki manages office operations.

The company sells and services a broad range of weighing equipment — from bench and floor scales to truck and rail scales — as well as meat processing machinery such as grinders, mixers, slicers, smokers, vacuum packers, and associated supplies. Its technicians are licensed in Montana and Wyoming to perform scale calibration, certification, repair, and placement-in-service reporting. The firm also provides equipment installation, repair, knife and grinder-plate sharpening, and acts as an authorized service representative for multiple brands.

Customers include meat processors, delis, ranchers, grocers, farmers’ markets, taxidermists, industrial plants, and individual buyers throughout Montana and Wyoming. The company participates in regional groups such as the Montana Meat Processors Association and the Montana Taxidermist Association.

B & L Scales emphasizes hands-on, on-site support — traveling to customers for delivery, installation, and service — and promotes the policy of servicing equipment regardless of where it was purchased.

name: B&M International Steel Company
old_description: Your Trusted Partner for Steel Fabrication, Erection, Detailing, Scanning & More
about:
B&M International Steel Company operates from Haymarket, Virginia, in the Northern Virginia corridor. The company was founded in 2013 and is family-owned and operated, with leadership including CEO Adam Brin and COO Stefan Brin. The Brin family directs a team that combines decades of combined industry experience across fabrication, erection, detailing, and project management.

The shop provides structural steel fabrication, steel erection, structural detailing, 3D laser point scanning, and building information modeling (BIM) with 3D and 4D capabilities. Services span from initial detailing and scanning through fabrication and on-site erection for projects throughout the Mid-Atlantic region. The company emphasizes precision fabrication and the use of advanced modeling software to coordinate complex builds.

Customers include general contractors, architects, and project managers on commercial construction projects across the Mid-Atlantic. The firm has delivered work for a range of building types, though specific project references are not published. Its project portfolio map highlights locations in Virginia, Maryland, and the District of Columbia.

B&M International Steel cites four pillars that distinguish its approach: decades of combined expertise among its personnel, precision driven by advanced scanning and modeling technology, reliable on-time delivery, and customer-centric solutions tailored to each project's requirements. The company states that its family-owned structure reinforces long-term client relationships and accountability.

about:
B & M Sheet Metal Shop, Inc. has been a family-owned fixture in Roanoke, Virginia since 1955. The company was founded by Wallace Leedy Martin, Edith Martin, and Marion Bartley, later run for decades by Wallace Lee Martin and now led by Luke McVey Martin.

The shop provides custom sheet metal fabrication services including laser cutting, press brake bending, welding, shearing, and plasma cutting. It produces ductwork, commercial kitchen hoods, and refurbishes stainless steel elevators, while also stocking a range of metals such as stainless steel, carbon steel, aluminum, galvanized, galvanneal, copper, and brass in sheet, flat bar, angle, tubing, and rod forms. The facility handles measuring, fabrication, and installation for most projects.

As a Class A Virginia contractor, B & M serves construction and commercial clients needing custom metalwork for building systems, food-service equipment, and elevator interiors. The company works from customer measurements and provides quotes before fabrication begins.

The business emphasizes its long-standing local presence, SWAM small-business certification, and registration with the U.S. State Department as differentiators in the regional market.
